scan.description: Two objects: target_box_translate (on boresight, oscillates x by +/-1m, rough/diffuse material) and target_box_rotate (off-boresight ~31deg, rotates in place +/-0.6rad yaw, specular material, zero translation). The center beam only sees the translating box, so its behavior matches dynamic_cpu's single-box scenario.

points.description: Combined point cloud bbox spans both objects. x midpoint moves less than in dynamic_cpu (diluted by the off-center, non-translating second object) but y midpoint now moves too -- that's specifically the rotating box's footprint changing, a signal the single-box scenario has no way to produce.

image.description: Center column still tracks only the translating box (peak row span matches dynamic_cpu almost exactly). The whole-image nonzero pixel count now swings much more (span ~70k vs ~0 in the static scenario) because the rotating box's specular material sweeps through and away from normal incidence as it yaws -- back_reflection_shader depends on incidence angle, so this is a real physics signal, not just a geometry-visibility one.
